name: QrCodeGenerator
src_typeComment: Dependency-free QR code encoder (ISO/IEC 18004), producing a Texture2D — no external library, no camera/ scanner integration needed, for "scan to continue on your phone" kiosk flows. Scope: versions 1-4, Error Correction Level M only (see QrVersionInfo's own comment for why), Alphanumeric or Byte mode auto-selected.  HONEST VERIFICATION CAVEAT (read this before trusting a generated code in production): this session has no way to render or camera-scan a QR code to confirm it decodes on a real phone. What IS verified by the self-test: the Reed-Solomon EC math against known GF(256) properties, the data bit-stream construction against the ISO 18004 Annex I published worked example ("HELLO WORLD", Version 1-M), and the format-info BCH computation's self-consistency. What is NOT independently verified: the exact module-placement coordinates (finder/timing/alignment/format-info exact positions) match the spec bit-for-bit — those were written from best-effort recall of the standard algorithm, not copied from a checked reference. Scan-test the first code this generates with a real phone before relying on it for anything user-facing.

src_members.name: GenerateMatrix
src_members.comment: Returns the raw module matrix (true = dark) — use this if you want to render it yourself (e.g. a custom mesh instead of a Texture2D).

src_members.sig: public static Texture2D GenerateTexture(string text, int pixelsPerModule = 8, int quietZoneModules = 4)
src_members.name: GenerateTexture
src_members.comment: Renders the matrix to a Texture2D — quiet zone (a mandatory blank border, ISO/IEC 18004 section 6.3.8) included, since a scanner may fail to lock onto a code with no margin. `pixelsPerModule` controls output resolution; `quietZoneModules` defaults to the spec's minimum of 4.
